title: Heart Failure Exacerbation
scenario: A 68-year-old female client with a history of chronic heart failure presents to the emergency department with worsening shortness of breath and swelling in both legs over the past three days.

lines: 68-year-old female brought in by daughter for 3 days of worsening dyspnea and bilateral lower-extremity edema. Reports sleeping in a recliner because she cannot lie flat. Bibasilar crackles on auscultation. Jugular venous distension noted. Weight up 4 kg from baseline. Alert and oriented x3.
IV access obtained. Labs and chest x-ray ordered. 2L O2 started per nasal cannula. Cardiac monitor applied.
IV furosemide administered per order. Foley catheter inserted to monitor output.
Reports breathing is easier. Crackles diminished at the bases. Voided 900 mL clear yellow urine since furosemide.
Insert indwelling urinary catheter, monitor strict intake and output
Notify provider for urine output < 30 mL/hr

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.rationale: Crackles, hypoxia, rapid weight gain, and JVD all indicate fluid volume overload from decompensated heart failure and require prompt intervention.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each finding, click to specify whether it supports left-sided heart failure, right-sided heart failure, or both. Each finding may support more than one.
children.rationale: Pulmonary congestion (crackles) reflects left-sided failure; systemic congestion (edema, JVD) reflects right-sided failure. BNP rises with either.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Complete the sentence. The nurse determines that the priority problem is {1}.

choices.text: impaired gas exchange from fluid overload

children.rationale: The most immediate threat is impaired gas exchange from pulmonary congestion, evidenced by hypoxia and crackles; it takes priority over the other real but less urgent problems.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each intervention, click to specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated for this client.

rows.text: Administer a rapid IV fluid bolus

children.rationale: Diuresis, upright positioning, and daily weights manage volume overload. Fluid boluses and high sodium worsen it and are contraindicated.

children.subject: Pharmacology
children.stem: After administering IV furosemide, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Restrict all oral fluids to zero

children.rationale: Loop diuretics cause potassium loss, diuresis, and possible hypotension, so the nurse monitors electrolytes, output, and blood pressure. Total fluid restriction and holding cardiac meds are not indicated.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Which findings indicate the treatment has been effective? Select all that apply.
children.rationale: Improved respiratory rate, oxygenation, breath sounds, and diuresis all show the fluid overload is resolving. Continued weight gain would signal worsening, not improvement.
